subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In OCR GCSE (9-1) Music (J536), the Practical Component is officially known as which component?
options: Component 01
Component 02
Component 03
Component 04
questions.explain: The Practical Component is Component 02, comprising an ensemble performance and a composition to an OCR-set brief.

questions.q: What proportion of the total GCSE mark is the Practical Component worth?
questions.explain: The Practical Component contributes 30% of the qualification, matching the 30% of the Integrated Portfolio.

questions.q: The performance submitted for the Practical Component must be which type?
options: A solo performance
An ensemble performance
An improvisation only
A conducted rehearsal
questions.explain: Component 02 requires an ensemble performance, distinct from the solo performance in Component 01.

questions.q: For a valid ensemble performance, the learner must perform in which arrangement?
options: Entirely alone
As part of a group of two or more performers
With only a pre-recorded backing track
In front of a live audience of ten or more
questions.explain: An ensemble requires the learner to perform as part of a group of two or more, with at least one other live performer.

questions.q: What is the minimum duration of the ensemble performance?
options: 30 seconds
1 minute
2 minutes
4 minutes
questions.explain: Each individual performance must last at least one minute, with the combined performance time reaching a minimum of four minutes.

questions.q: Who sets the brief for the composition in the Practical Component?
options: The learner
The class teacher
OCR
An external moderator
questions.explain: The Practical Component composition responds to a brief set by OCR, unlike the learner's own brief used in Component 01.

questions.q: The OCR-set composition briefs are each linked to one of which set of options?
options: The five areas of study
The three assessed components
The four listening exam papers
The graded difficulty levels
questions.explain: Each set brief is tied to one of the five areas of study, giving learners a stylistic starting point for composing.

questions.q: Out of how many marks is each individual performance and each composition assessed?
options: 20 marks
30 marks
40 marks
60 marks
questions.explain: Each performance and each composition is marked out of 30, so Component 02 totals 60 marks.

questions.q: Why should the learner's part in an ensemble not simply double another performer's part in unison throughout?
options: It would make the piece too loud
The learner's individual contribution could not be clearly assessed
Unison playing is banned by OCR
It would exceed the time limit
questions.explain: The learner needs a distinct, independent part so the moderator can assess their own musical contribution.

questions.q: How does the Practical Component composition differ from the composition in the Integrated Portfolio?
options: It must be for solo voice only
It responds to an OCR-set brief rather than the learner's own brief
It does not need a recording
It is worth twice as many marks
questions.explain: Component 01's composition uses the learner's own brief, while Component 02's composition answers a brief set by OCR.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of composing to a set brief?
options: To copy an existing published work
To demonstrate the ability to respond to given musical parameters and stimuli
To avoid using any notation
To perform live without preparation
questions.explain: A set brief tests whether a learner can shape original music to meet specified requirements, purpose and style.

questions.q: The combined performance time across both components must total at least four minutes. What does this mean for a single performance?
options: Every single performance must last four minutes
Each performance must be at least one minute, and together they reach four minutes
Only one performance is needed in total
Performances shorter than four minutes score zero
questions.explain: Each performance must last a minimum of one minute, with the two performances combining to at least four minutes.

questions.q: What must be submitted alongside a completed composition?
options: A recording only
A recording plus a score or written account of the piece
A live re-performance
A written listening exam
questions.explain: Compositions are submitted with a recording together with a score or a written account documenting the music.

questions.q: Why does performing over only a pre-recorded backing track not usually qualify as an ensemble?
options: Backing tracks are not allowed at all
An ensemble requires at least one other live performer
The recording quality is too low
It would be too short
questions.explain: An ensemble needs interaction with at least one other live performer, which a backing track alone does not provide.

questions.q: A set brief typically provides which kind of information to guide a learner's composition?
options: The exact notes to write down
A stimulus with parameters such as intended purpose, style and musical requirements
A recording to copy exactly
The final mark before submission
questions.explain: Briefs supply a creative stimulus and constraints, leaving the actual musical content for the learner to compose.

questions.q: A learner plays flute in exact unison with another flute for the whole piece. Why is this problematic for the ensemble assessment?
options: The piece is too demanding
Their part is not independent, so their individual contribution is hard to assess
Two flutes cannot form an ensemble
Unison playing scores full marks automatically
questions.explain: Without a distinct line, the moderator cannot judge the learner's own performance, weakening the ensemble evidence.

questions.q: A learner selects a set brief linked to Film Music. Which response best fits the brief?
options: A four-bar folk melody for solo recorder
Music to underscore a tense on-screen chase scene
A note-for-note copy of a pop chart hit
A written essay about a composer
questions.explain: A Film Music brief calls for original music that supports a filmic mood or scene, such as a tense chase.

questions.q: A learner's solo lasts one minute and their ensemble lasts one minute, giving two minutes in total. Does this meet the performance requirements?
options: Yes, each performance meets the minimum
No, the combined performance time must be at least four minutes
Yes, because there are two performances
No, because solos are not permitted
questions.explain: Although each performance clears the one-minute minimum, the two together must total at least four minutes.

questions.q: A learner performs a very simple piece that is well below the standard level of demand, but plays it accurately. What is the likely consequence?
options: Full marks, because it is accurate
The marks available may be limited because the music is less demanding than the standard level
The performance is disqualified entirely
The time requirement is waived
questions.explain: OCR takes the level of demand into account, so music below the standard level restricts the marks that can be accessed.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Music (J536) specification; Component: Practical Component
